dimensions.label: Speed and tempo
dimensions.definition: how fast an activity is done or a change takes place.

dimensions.label: Duration and horizon
dimensions.definition: how long an activity, a state or an effect lasts.

dimensions.label: Sequence and order
dimensions.definition: the order in which activities or events occur.

dimensions.label: Rhythm, cycle and entrainment
dimensions.definition: the recurrence of an activity at a pattern of intervals; one complete recurrence; the adjustment of one rhythm to another, so that the two keep step.

dimensions.label: Timing
dimensions.definition: when an activity or event takes place, relative to the clock, to a calendar or to other events.

dimensions.label: Trajectory and path
dimensions.definition: the course that a quantity or a relationship follows over time.

conceptions.name: Clock time
conceptions.definition: time measured in uniform, divisible units, independent of the events that fill it.

conceptions.name: Process time
conceptions.definition: time counted by events and activities, such as episodes of use, and not by the clock.

conceptions.name: A-series time
conceptions.definition: time as past, present and future, in which events pass from future to past.

conceptions.name: B-series time
conceptions.definition: time as the order of earlier and later, which does not change.

conceptions.name: World time
conceptions.definition: time as people meet it in what they are doing, as the time for something.

conceptions.name: Time as a resource
conceptions.definition: time as a scarce means that people allocate and spend.

conceptions.name: Time as a structure
conceptions.definition: time as the schedules, cycles and patterns that order activity.

conceptions.name: Time as a process
conceptions.definition: time as the continuing unfolding of events.

conceptions.name: Temporal work
conceptions.definition: the work people do to construct and reconcile accounts of past, present and future.

conceptions.name: Ambitemporality
conceptions.definition: holding more than one temporal orientation or conception at once.

auditQuestions.duration: does the theory state the interval over which the relationship holds?
auditQuestions.sequence: does it give an order among the constructs the relationship joins?
auditQuestions.rhythm: does it name a cycle in which the relationship recurs?
auditQuestions.timing: does it say when the effect is expected?
auditQuestions.speed: does it say how fast the cause produces the effect?
auditQuestions.trajectory: does it state the path the relationship follows over time?

admissibleChanges: introduction or removal of a mediator
introduction or removal of a moderator
a new path between constructs already in the theory
transformCriteria: M is specific and interpretable in the theory's vocabulary and at its level.
R′ is detectable with established instruments.
Temporal check: M follows from C and would not arise without it.
C uses the words of the drawn cell of Table S1 and its scale.
